findings.title: Call to nonexistent no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: The condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in this PR (protected, in UsernamePasswordForm) takes a `UserModel` parameter, and no no-arg overload appears in the shown code. The services module will not compile, so nothing in the PR can be built or tested. It should pass the user, i.e. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or use the helper as intended.

findings.title: Passkey conditional UI is no longer set up on the initial login page
findings.body: The passkey fill was moved out of the `user == null` branch and is now guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. That helper (lines 160-162) returns `webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so it is false whenever no user has been identified yet. The normal first login page therefore never gets `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`, and the webauth form and 'username webauthn' autocomplete disappear. Existing tests that expect these on the first page will fail, e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (around line 145-146) and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (line 192). The fill must run both when the user is unknown and when it is already set, so these call sites should check only `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`.

findings.title: Passkey UI dropped when the username/password challenge is re-rendered with an error and no user is set
findings.body: `challenge(context, error, field)` now gates the webauthn fill with `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which is false when no user is set. Before this PR the fill ran exactly when `context.getUser() == null`. That is the case for an invalid username on the conditional-UI page, which reaches this method through testInvalidUser/getUserFromForm. After this change the error page is rendered without the webauthn setup, so the passkey autofill and 'username webauthn' autocomplete are lost after the first failed username. This is the same root cause as the line 115 regression and needs the same fix.

findings.title: configureTestRealm() call has no definition visible in this change
findings.body: `configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation)` is newly called here, but the method is neither defined in this file nor added by the diff. If it is not inherited from AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest or another base class with a matching signature, the test module will not compile. This should be verified.

findings.title: No test covers a failed passkey attempt during re-authentication
findings.body: createErrorResponse now calls setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError, which changes the page shown when a passkey fails for a user already set in the flow (username hidden, registration disabled). None of the added tests exercise this path. They cover wrong-password followed by passkey success, but never a failed passkey during a prompt=login re-authentication. A test should fail a passkey in that flow and assert the username field is hidden and the error is shown.
